body:
## Why

`scripts/ci_coverage_delta.py:20-26` (`_parse_float`) returns `float(value)` for any parseable string, and `scripts/ci_coverage_delta.py:59-72` (`_build_payload`) computes `drop = max(0.0, baseline - current) if baseline > 0 else 0.0` and then `if baseline <= 0 ... elif drop == 0: status = "ok"`. Every ordered comparison with NaN is False, so a NaN baseline yields `drop = 0.0` and `status = "ok"` with `should_fail = False`. `_extract_line_rate` at `scripts/ci_coverage_delta.py:35-48` accepts `line-rate="nan"` the same way, and `max(0.0, baseline - nan)` is `0.0`, so a NaN current coverage also reports `ok`.

Executed at tip `e4b6adecb7cee6750b37d697d2c487153678e0a2` (2026-09-13):

- `_build_payload(75.0, float('nan'), 1.0, fail_on_drop=True)` -> status `ok`, `should_fail False`
- `_build_payload(float('nan'), 75.0, 1.0, fail_on_drop=True)` -> status `ok`, `should_fail False`
- control `_build_payload(70.0, 75.0, 1.0, fail_on_drop=True)` -> status `fail`, `should_fail True`

The upstream guard does not close this. `.github/workflows/reusable-10-ci-python.yml:270-292` (`validate_number`) rejects with `value < min_value` and `value > max_value`; for NaN both are False, so `baseline-coverage: nan` and `coverage-alert-drop: nan` pass the `validate-inputs` job (`.github/workflows/reusable-10-ci-python.yml:334-345`) and reach `scripts/ci_coverage_delta.py` through `.github/workflows/reusable-10-ci-python.yml:2446-2452`. A replica of `validate_number` confirms: `nan` -> accept, `inf` -> reject (> max), `-10` -> reject (< min). Negative and over-100 values are therefore already blocked at the live wiring, and only the NaN path is a current fail-open of a consumer's `fail-on-coverage-drop: true` gate.

Same class in the sibling synced script: `scripts/ci_metrics.py:56-65` (`_parse_float`) rejects only `parsed < 0`, so `inf` and `nan` pass; `scripts/ci_metrics.py:171-175` (`_collect_slow_tests`) then returns `[]` for every case and `json.dumps` emits non-standard `NaN` in `threshold_seconds`. Executed: `_collect_slow_tests(cases, top_n=5, min_seconds=float('inf'))` -> `[]`, `min_seconds=float('nan')` -> `[]`. Its live wiring is guarded because `slow-test-min-seconds` is parsed with `int()` at `.github/workflows/reusable-10-ci-python.yml:327-333`, so this part is latent and is included only because it is the same three-line fix in the same workflow's second synced script.

## Scope

- `scripts/ci_coverage_delta.py` — `_parse_float`, `_extract_line_rate`.
- `scripts/ci_metrics.py` — `_parse_float`, non-finite testcase durations.
- `.github/workflows/reusable-10-ci-python.yml` — `validate_number` in the `validate-inputs` step.
- `tests/scripts/test_ci_coverage_delta.py`, `tests/scripts/test_ci_metrics.py`.

## Implementation Notes

- Both scripts are consumer-synced single files (`.github/sync-manifest.yml:293-299`) executed from the consumer's checkout at `.github/workflows/reusable-10-ci-python.yml:2371` and `.github/workflows/reusable-10-ci-python.yml:2446`. Validate inline with stdlib `math.isfinite`; do NOT introduce a shared helper module imported by these scripts, because a consumer would receive an import of a file it does not have until a later sync batch.
- `scripts/ci_coverage_delta.py`: give `_parse_float` keyword bounds (`minimum`, `maximum`) and raise `SystemExit` naming the env var when the value is non-finite or out of range; call it with 0..100 for `BASELINE_COVERAGE` and finite non-negative for `ALERT_DROP`. In `_extract_line_rate`, reject a non-finite rate or one outside 0..1 before multiplying by 100. `_build_payload` needs no logic change once its inputs are finite; keep `test_build_payload_status_matrix` passing.
- `scripts/ci_metrics.py`: add the `math.isfinite` check to `_parse_float`; in `_extract_testcases`, treat a non-finite `time` the way an unparseable one is already treated (see `tests/scripts/test_ci_metrics.py::test_extract_testcases_handles_invalid_time_and_prioritizes_status`).
- `.github/workflows/reusable-10-ci-python.yml`: inside `validate_number`, after parsing, add `if not math.isfinite(value): fail(...)` (import `math` at the top of the heredoc). Editing a workflow file may require the `agents:allow-change` label per `docs/AGENTS_POLICY.md`; the two script changes stand on their own if the workflow edit lands separately.
- `.github/workflows/selftest-reusable-ci.yml:270-286` already drives `scripts/ci_coverage_delta.py` with `baseline-coverage: "65"`; it must keep passing.

## Tasks

- [ ] Reject non-finite and out-of-range values in `_parse_float` and `_extract_line_rate` in `scripts/ci_coverage_delta.py` (baseline 0..100, alert drop finite and non-negative, line-rate 0..1) with a `SystemExit` message that names the variable.
- [ ] Reject non-finite `MIN_SECONDS` in `_parse_float` in `scripts/ci_metrics.py` and drop or zero non-finite testcase durations in `_extract_testcases` before `_collect_slow_tests` builds the payload.
- [ ] Add a `math.isfinite` rejection to `validate_number` in the `validate-inputs` step of `.github/workflows/reusable-10-ci-python.yml` so `nan` fails input validation for every numeric input.
- [ ] Add `test_parse_float_rejects_non_finite_values`, `test_parse_float_rejects_out_of_range_values`, and `test_extract_line_rate_rejects_non_finite_rate` to `tests/scripts/test_ci_coverage_delta.py`.
- [ ] Add `test_parse_float_rejects_non_finite_values` parametrised over `nan`, `inf`, `-inf` to `tests/scripts/test_ci_metrics.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `pytest tests/scripts/test_ci_coverage_delta.py tests/scripts/test_ci_metrics.py` passes, including `tests/scripts/test_ci_coverage_delta.py::test_parse_float_rejects_non_finite_values`, which asserts `_parse_float("nan", "BASELINE_COVERAGE", 0.0)` raises `SystemExit` with `BASELINE_COVERAGE` in the message.
- `tests/scripts/test_ci_coverage_delta.py::test_extract_line_rate_rejects_non_finite_rate` asserts a `coverage.xml` with `line-rate="nan"` makes `_extract_line_rate` raise `SystemExit` instead of returning a value that `_build_payload` would grade `ok`.
- With `BASELINE_COVERAGE=nan FAIL_ON_DROP=true` and a `coverage.xml` whose `line-rate` is `0.70`, `python scripts/ci_coverage_delta.py` exits non-zero and writes no `coverage-delta.json` with `status` equal to `ok`.
- `tests/scripts/test_ci_coverage_delta.py::test_build_payload_status_matrix` and `tests/scripts/test_ci_metrics.py::test_parse_helpers_validate_non_negative` still pass unchanged.
- Deliberate break: temporarily remove the `math.isfinite` check from `_parse_float` in `scripts/ci_coverage_delta.py`, confirm `tests/scripts/test_ci_coverage_delta.py::test_parse_float_rejects_non_finite_values` fails, then revert.

## Non-Goals

- No shared numeric-parsing helper module; the synced scripts stay single-file.
- No change to `scripts/workflow_health_check.py` (no workflow invokes it) or `scripts/workflow_startup_failure_diagnostic.py` (its invalid values already raise at the first request).
- No change to the integer contract of `slow-test-min-seconds` or to `_truthy` in `scripts/ci_coverage_delta.py` and `scripts/ci_history.py`.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: adding the tests or the workflow-level `math.isfinite` check while `_build_payload` in `scripts/ci_coverage_delta.py` stays reachable with a NaN baseline or NaN line-rate (the script is also run directly by `.github/workflows/selftest-reusable-ci.yml` and by local invocations) is a failure of this issue.
title: [P2] Coverage-drop gate fails open on NaN: baseline-coverage=nan passes reusable-10 input validation and ci_coverage_delta reports ok
